articles.headline: Cabinet approves the VISTAR scheme to upgrade India's official statistical system
articles.relevance: National scheme, ministry, acronym, outlay and scheme period are suitable for general-awareness revision.
articles.summary: On 4 November 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR), a Central Sector Scheme for FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31, with an outlay of ₹4,371.10 crore. The stated objective is to strengthen the official statistical system through more timely, granular, interoperable and AI-ready data, alongside survey execution, methodological research and digital transformation.
keyFacts: Full form: Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research.
Administrative scope: statistical and data-management activities of MoSPI.

articles.headline: Cabinet approves ₹14,500-crore VGF scheme for 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage
articles.relevance: Useful national energy-policy figures and basic distinctions between pumped storage and battery storage.
articles.summary: On 4 November 2026, the Union Cabinet approved a Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme with total financial support of ₹14,500 crore for the development of 92 GWh of yet-to-be-commissioned grid-scale energy-storage capacity during FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31. The planned mix is 60 GWh of pumped-storage projects, 30 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and 2 GWh through emerging storage technologies.
keyFacts: Scheme: Viability Gap Funding (VGF) Scheme for Development of Grid-Scale Energy Storage Systems.
Break-up: 60 GWh pumped storage, 30 GWh BESS, 2 GWh emerging technologies.

articles.headline: Cabinet approves ₹2,814-crore support scheme for domestic lithium and nickel processing
articles.relevance: Useful for critical minerals, domestic processing, clean-energy supply chains and scheme figures.
articles.summary: On 4 November 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing, with a financial outlay of ₹2,814 crore over FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31. The scheme provides a capital subsidy of 30% of eligible investment for four processing plants: two lithium plants with a minimum capacity of 30 kt each and two nickel plants with a minimum capacity of 50 kt each. Cobalt is expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production.
keyFacts: Four plants: two lithium plants (minimum 30 kt each) and two nickel plants (minimum 50 kt each).
Cobalt is expected as a by-product of nickel production; the scheme's named processing targets are lithium and nickel.

articles.headline: Cabinet extends the Fast Track Special Courts scheme for five more years
articles.relevance: A major Central Sector/Centrally Sponsored justice initiative with a clear duration, outlay and target number of courts.
articles.summary: On 4 November 2026, the Union Cabinet approved continuation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive POCSO Courts, for five years from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. The total financial outlay is ₹3,788.04 crore. The extended scheme provides for 850 FTSCs, including exclusive POCSO Courts, across participating States and Union Territories.

articles.headline: Indian Railways records 145.07 million tonnes of freight loading in October 2026
articles.relevance: Directly relevant to RRB railway awareness and useful for SSC current-affairs figures.
articles.summary: The Ministry of Railways reported that Indian Railways loaded 145.07 million tonnes of freight in October 2026, its highest-ever freight loading for an October. The comparable figure for October 2025 was 133.93 million tonnes, so the reported year-on-year increase was 8.32%. For April–October 2026, cumulative freight loading was 978.78 million tonnes, up 4.67% from 935.10 million tonnes in the corresponding period a year earlier.
keyFacts: April–October 2026 cumulative freight loading: 978.78 million tonnes.

articles.headline: DRDO successfully flight-tests the quasi-ballistic missile Pralay off the Odisha coast
articles.relevance: Defence technology and missile classification are recurring general-awareness themes.
articles.summary: On 5 November 2026, the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) successfully flight-tested the indigenously developed quasi-ballistic missile Pralay from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the Odisha coast, at about 11:10 a.m., as part of user-evaluation trials. The Ministry of Defence said all test objectives were met. Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad, along with other DRDO laboratories, developed the missile; Bharat Dynamics Limited was one of the Development-cum-Production Partners and produced the system.
keyFacts: Test location: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the Odisha coast.
Development: Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad, with other DRDO laboratories.
Production partner named in the release: Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL).

articles.headline: MoPNG reports 893 E20 petrol samples from 27 States and UTs within the prescribed ethanol range
articles.relevance: A current fuel-standard and energy-blending fact with exact sample count, coverage and BIS standard.
articles.summary: In a 7 November 2026 release, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas reported that an OMC/Centre for High Technology Quality Coordination Cell exercise tested 893 E20 samples drawn from depots and retail outlets across 27 States and Union Territories. The Ministry stated that all 893 samples were within the prescribed ethanol-content range of 19–21%, tested under IS 17021, Annex C. The 893 samples comprised 330 from IOCL, 280 from BPCL and 283 from HPCL. This is a statement about the sampled set, not a claim that every retail outlet was tested.
keyFacts: Reported ethanol-content range: 19–21% across the 893 samples.
Test reference: IS 17021, Annex C; BIS catalogues IS 17021:2018 as the E20 fuel specification.
